title: Hand-Arm Vibration
whatItIs: Regular use of vibrating tools like breakers, grinders and sanders can cause hand-arm vibration syndrome (HAVS) and carpal tunnel syndrome. The damage is largely permanent.
keyFacts: HAVS signs: tingling and numbness in the fingers, weaker grip, fingers going white then red and painful.

keyFacts.text: At or above the action value of 2.5 m/s² A(8), employers MUST reduce exposure as low as reasonably practicable.
Employers MUST NOT let anyone's daily exposure go above the limit value of 5 m/s² A(8).
Employers MUST provide suitable health surveillance for workers likely to be exposed at or above the action value.

keyFacts: Gloves and warm clothing help blood flow, but gloves give no protection from vibration itself.
Keep tools maintained: blunt, worn or loose parts make more vibration and jobs take longer.

visual.caption: Vibration values and rough times to reach them (regular daily use)

rows: Clear risk: must be managed and reduced
High risk: must not be exceeded
notes: HSE's rough guide for modern, well-maintained tools. Old or damaged tools can be worse.

a.label: Hand-arm vibration syndrome
points: Tingling and numbness in the fingers
Fingers go white, then red and painful

b.label: Carpal tunnel syndrome
points: Tingling, numbness, pain and weakness in the hand
Can also be caused by vibration

onTheTest.question: Which is an early sign of hand-arm vibration syndrome?
options: Tingling and numbness in the fingers
A red, itchy rash on the forearms
onTheTest.why: HSE INDG175: HAVS symptoms include tingling and numbness in the fingers, weaker grip and white fingers.

onTheTest.question: What is the daily exposure limit value for hand-arm vibration?
onTheTest.why: Vibration Regulations reg 4(1): daily limit value 5 m/s² A(8); action value 2.5 m/s² A(8).

traps: Gloves keep your hands warm but don't stop vibration.
A tighter grip passes more vibration into your hands.
Cold and smoking make it worse: they reduce blood flow to the fingers.
Don't ignore tingling: the damage is largely irreversible.
